segments.line: You do the math
A quarter of a tank is about a hundred and fifty kilometers
The war in the east is more than two thousand kilometers away
The car will die in the desert
And so will you the moment the emperor finds out it's useless
But the tunnel the place where you arrived is only forty kilometers south
Maybe it still works Maybe it doesn't
And if it doesn't you've burned your last fuel for nothing
Then someone knocks It's Apollodorus He shuts the door and whispers
'An emperor with a horseless chariot would never stop making war Go home.'
He gives you a key And a map of the palace
You find Mo locked in a storeroom eating grapes
'Took you long enough,' he says
You push the car out of the courtyard in silence headlights off
At the bottom of the hill you start the engine
Somewhere above you a guard shouts
You race through the dark streets past sleeping bakeries and empty markets
with Mo reading the map by the light of his phone
At the city gate the same soldiers from day one see you coming
This time they don't even raise their spears
They just step aside
Horses A lot of horses
On a smooth highway you'd leave them behind in seconds
But this is a Roman road made of big stone blocks and every bump could break the car
So you do the one thing they've never seen
You switch on the high beams
The horses rear The riders go flying
And you race south on the Appian Way in the dark on the last of your fuel
